title: Make bd child creation impossible to collide or silently succeed
what_this_does: Today bd picks the number for a new child issue from a side table that only one code path keeps up to date, and never checks which numbers are actually in use. When that table falls behind, bd hands out a number that already belongs to another issue, and the insert quietly does nothing while reporting success, so the new issue's parent link and blockers land on the old issue instead. This change makes the issues table the authority on which numbers are taken, keeps the side table only as a floor that never moves backwards, and does the whole child creation in one database transaction that fails loudly instead of writing nothing. It also makes every insert in bd strict, which repairs a second bug where importing a renamed issue deleted the old row and wrote nothing in its place.
why_bother: A farmplanner agent lost an afternoon to this on 9 September: it wired a live epic's blocker onto a closed bug and had to unpick the damage by hand, and the same database still has ten numbers of drift waiting to do it again. Every repo on this machine runs the same binary.

flow.label: Find which numbers are taken
flow.detail: Read the highest existing child of this parent from the issues table, alongside the floor, and take whichever is larger plus one. Closed and deleted-but-tombstoned children still count.

flow.label: Create the issue and its parent link together
flow.detail: One transaction inserts the row, raises the floor to the number just used, records the event and adds the parent link. Anything that fails rolls all of it back.

flow.label: Refuse to write nothing
flow.detail: Inserts stop using the silent ignore-if-present form, so a create that collides now fails with a message naming the ID instead of reporting success.

flow.label: Prove it on a real database
flow.detail: Thirteen checks run against a freshly built binary, including the exact farmplanner shape, eight concurrent creates, and a database whose floor has been forced backwards.

flow.label: Replace the fleet binary
flow.detail: Build with the commit stamped in, rename it over the copy at ~/.local/libexec/bd-real so running agents keep the old file, then verify the installed binary reports the merged commit.

flow.label: Decide
flow.detail: Approve or send back through the rail on this page.

approving.plain: The issues table decides which child numbers are free, and the counter table survives only as a floor that never drops.
approving.detail: allocateChildNumber reads max(floor, highest existing immediate child) + 1 and writes nothing. The floor is kept because tombstones expire after 30 days (internal/types/types.go:152) and rows can be deleted outright, so a number whose issue has gone from this database may still exist in git history or a peer's copy, and reusing it would collide on the next sync. The counter is raised by every function that writes an issue row, and there are three: the two insert helpers and multi-repo hydration, which writes rows on every store open under a multi-repo config.

approving.plain: Creating a child becomes a single database operation, so the issue and its parent link can never exist without each other.
approving.detail: CreateChildIssue runs inside one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction and replaces GetNextChildID in the storage interface, which removes the ability to reserve a number without writing the row. Both the command line and the daemon call it, so the two paths stop diverging.

approving.plain: Every insert becomes strict, so no create in bd can report success without writing a row.
approving.detail: insertIssue, insertIssues and multi-repo hydration's upsertIssueInTx all drop the silent ignore-if-present form. This also repairs a data-loss race: the importer renames by deleting the old row and then creating the new one in a separate transaction, and if another clone writes the target in between, today's silent insert leaves the old row deleted and nothing written, because the recovery branch at internal/importer/importer.go:472 cannot fire on an error the create never returns.

approving.plain: Naming an issue's own ID and its parent in the same command becomes legal when the two agree.
approving.detail: The mutual exclusion existed only because the parent flag overwrote the supplied ID (cmd/bd/create.go:151). A mismatch is now an error raised before anything is written. This removes the workaround the farmplanner agent had to use.

approving.plain: One existing behaviour becomes stricter: creating an epic underneath a non-epic now fails instead of warning.
approving.detail: The parent-link direction check moves inside the transaction, so what was a warning nobody read (cmd/bd/create.go:318) becomes a create that writes nothing. Ship gate row 12 covers it.

approving.plain: The fleet binary is replaced as part of this work, not left for later.
approving.detail: The build stamps the commit through ldflags, which is the only way bd version --json reports one, and the new file is renamed into place so agents mid-command keep running the old one.

rejected.idea: Drop the counter table and trust the issues table alone
rejected.why: Tombstones expire and rows can be deleted, so the highest surviving child is not the highest number ever used. The next create would reissue a dead child's number and collide with the copy still in git history.

rejected.idea: Keep the counter authoritative and add a migration that repairs every stale row
rejected.why: It fixes today's databases and does nothing about tomorrow's import, which creates children without touching the counter. The repair has to live in the allocation path, not in a one-off.

rejected.idea: Raise the floor only where children are allocated by the parent flag
rejected.why: That protects exactly the numbers a scan of the issues table would already find, and leaves an explicitly numbered child's number free to be reissued once its row is gone. The raise belongs at the insert, which every create passes through.

rejected.idea: Split the work so storage lands before its callers
rejected.why: Removing the allocation method from the interface breaks every caller in the same compile, so any split leaves a phase whose build gate cannot pass.

risks.risk: A path that writes issue rows without maintaining the floor leaves a number free to be reissued
risks.response: A fourth review round, by the agent that did the original diagnosis, found exactly that in multi-repo hydration after three rounds missed it. All three row writers now maintain the floor, each has a test, and the rule to check is recorded in CONTEXT.md.

risks.risk: The floor write breaks any import carrying an orphan child, because the counter's parent column is a foreign key and orphans are legal by default
risks.response: Measured, not assumed: the unguarded statement returns FOREIGN KEY constraint failed (19), so the statement carries a WHERE EXISTS guard that makes it a no-op for an absent parent. An importer test covers it.

risks.risk: Strict inserts wake the importer's dormant rename branch, changing import behaviour
risks.response: That branch is the intended recovery and it replaces silent deletion of the renamed issue. The collision error keeps the driver's own text so the branch still matches on it, and a test covers the case.

risks.risk: Removing checkForExistingIDs takes a guard off the import path
risks.response: EnsureIDs already rejects both in-batch duplicates and IDs present in the database, before any write, and runs immediately before the deleted call on the same batch. The strict insert closes the rest with an error naming the ID.

risks.risk: Replacing the binary while agents are running
risks.response: The build writes bd-real.new beside the target and renames it into place, so running processes keep the old inode and nobody sees a half-written file.
